Definition and entire equivalence argument checked. The solution is the specified representation-formula solution, with the exact regularity and data-attainment suppliers independently read; no unconditional energy uniqueness is inferred. Strong Huygens is invariance under neighbourhood agreement at the positive-radius sphere. Linear perturbations vanishing near S are cut off outside a slightly larger ball; base-ball locality keeps the functional unchanged, and the compact perturbation splits smoothly across its zero collar into an interior compact support and an exterior part vanishing near the closed base. This proves strictly-inside, shell and germ equivalence in both directions. Empty support gives zero; nonempty compact support missing S has positive distance from it. Bare restrictions are insufficient: the radial u0=(1−r)psi(r) has sphere value zero but normal derivative −1, yielding Kirchhoff value −1. Reader’s germ/jet distinction and exact uniqueness-class and attainment qualifications are accepted. Verification 1.1–3.1: odd displacement and velocity make the d’Alembert sum and oriented velocity integral odd in x, so the endpoint trace is zero. For incoming data phi,cphi′, FTC on intervals cut at zero yields phi(x+ct)−phi(ct−x) for 0<x<ct; for x>ct it is phi(x+ct), a left-moving incoming profile. Odd extensions are C²/C¹ because phi is compactly supported away from zero. U_t is odd, U_x is even, so energy density is even and half-line energy is half the whole-line value. For every finite T0, solution support lies in a fixed compact data-support-plus-interval set; conservation applies in the interior and uniform continuity extends it to endpoints. Countable Choice licenses the integral bridge. Reader direction, FTC and compact-cylinder repairs accepted.

Verification 1.1–3.1: sharp conserved energy zero is an explicit hypothesis, with differentiable u0 making its data-energy expression defined. Positive-time continuous nonnegative density plus positive ball measure gives zero first derivatives everywhere. Spatial constancy and the one-variable zero-derivative theorem give a single constant k in space-time. Pointwise Cauchy limits then give u0=k and u1=0, rather than trying to upgrade possibly discontinuous initial data from almost-everywhere values. Conversely every k is a classical zero-energy wave; k≠0 shows zero energy does not imply zero displacement. Reader reordered the argument and fixed initial-energy typing; accepted.

Proof 1.1–4.1 checked with the independently read odd representation proof and smoothness proof. After k−1 applications of D_t to t^(2k−1)g, terms have exponents 1+j and derivative order j≤k−1; one extra ordinary time derivative gives displacement radial order ≤k, while velocity uses ≤k−1. c^j comes from the composite radius ct and all needed finite derivatives are available. Sphere-normalized integral at positive time gives neighbourhood-germ invariance, not bare-restriction invariance. Nonempty compact K disjoint from the positive-radius sphere has a positive gap; empty K gives zero separately. If K is a radius-r ball, spheres miss it for |x−x0|<ct−r or |x−x0|>ct+r; support is therefore contained in the closed annulus, with no assertion of occupied boundaries. Reader’s sphere arguments, positive-time shell, empty-K and moving-front corrections accepted. decisions.evidence: Proof 1.1–3.1: d’Alembert’s velocity integral is nonzero for nonzero-integral compact data strictly inside the base interval. In even n=2k, support lies in a fixed epsilon-ball with epsilon<ct0; choose delta so c(t0−delta)>epsilon, giving a compact parameter majorant for all finitely many time derivatives. The kernel at zero is c^(−n)/(n!!V_n) times (−1)^(k−1)(2k−3)!! t0^(−(2k−1)), obtained by repeatedly lowering the exponent of t^(−1) by two. It is nonzero, with the empty product 1 for k=1. Continuity gives a fixed-sign collar and a translated nonnegative smooth bump makes the integral strictly nonzero by positive-ball measure and the zero-integral characterization. Zero data agree near the sphere, so this is actual failure of germ invariance. The odd theorem supplies the complementary dimensions. Reader sign-collar, construction and positivity citations accepted. Teschl §7.1 pp.171–172 provides the 2D/3D contrast, but the general even-dimensional kernel is (7.24), §7.2 p.175. Proof 1.1–3.1: translated smooth velocity bumps strictly inside the base interval/disk yield positive d’Alembert/Poisson values while zero data agree near the sphere. For smooth nonnegative displacement and zero velocity in n=2, differentiation on a fixed compact support with c²t²−r² bounded below gives coefficient −ct0/(2pi), hence a strictly negative centre value. This establishes failure of positivity preservation independently of Huygens and smoothing. All witnesses have compact support, with Countable Choice exactly for the integral machinery.
